rationale: The four-case experiment executed and was retained (CheckRun 62f089bd843641099558ff8d8831ab29, exit 0, tests_passed). It confirms the earlier local reading by measurement: the TrailingLogs=0 case loops, the (10,20) and (25,20) cases converge, and the backlog case met the compacted-boundary condition yet its peer converged with zero snapshot installs. This update records the measured interpretation, promotes the operands to a Fact, and states that the compaction condition is necessary but not sufficient.

knowledge.statement: Executed backlog case: divergent_prefix reports partitioned_leader_last_index 61, partner_last_index 46, partner_store 1..46 with trailing_logs 2; successor_snapshot reports snapshot_index 4, successor_applied_index 60, successor_last_index 63, successor_store_first 5 and successor_store_last 63, so the leader's retained log began above its own snapshot index; rejoin_observe then reports restores_before/early/late all 0, partner_applied_index 64 equal to successor_applied_index 64, partner_store 61..62 and successor_store 63..64. In the same receipt the (TrailingLogs=0, no post-snapshot entries) case loops with partner applied index 4, last index 7 and thousands of installs, while the (10,20) and (25,20) cases converge with restores 0 and indexes 24.
knowledge.conditions: One process, root package '.', MakeClusterCustom with five bootstrapped nodes over InmemTransport/InmemStore, two-sided partition of {leader, partner} from the other three peers; backlog case uses TrailingLogs=2, SnapshotThreshold=5, SnapshotInterval=10ms, a 15 ms-per-apply FSM and 60 uncommitted commands replicated to the peer before the heal. Frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df.

interpretations.rationale: The prediction under test was that a leader with non-zero TrailingLogs which snapshots under a real backlog, so that its retained log begins above the snapshot index, will leave a rejoining peer unrepairable. The retained receipt contradicts it, so the comparison is violated and that prediction is refuted. Parsed CheckRun 62f089bd843641099558ff8d8831ab29: index 35 shows the successor's snapshot at index 4 with successor_store_first 5 and store_last 63, i.e. the snapshot boundary was compacted away while the log extended 59 entries beyond it; index 43 shows rejoin_observe with restores_before/early/late all 0, partner_applied_index 64 equal to successor_applied_index 64, and partner_store 61..62 against successor_store 63..64. So the peer was repaired without any InstallSnapshot even though the boundary was gone, which refutes the compaction condition as a sufficient trigger and shows the TrailingLogs=0 loop cannot be generalised by it. The remaining unexplained element is that the peer's store (61..62) differs from the leader's (63..64) at the same applied index 64, and the peer applied 61 commands, which is consistent with the peer snapshotting on its own during catch-up under the same small SnapshotThreshold; that confound is recorded as the next discriminator rather than assumed. Scope of the finding is therefore unchanged and must be presented strictly as: with TrailingLogs=0 and a snapshot taken at the log end (single-peer witness CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7 and sealed-partition witness CheckRun f66fa4e4e0514f7e95b7788032144a30, cause isolated by CheckRun beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f). No claim is made that a non-zero trailing configuration reproduces the loop.
counterevidence: In the retained backlog case the peer reached the leader's applied index with zero snapshot installs although the retained log began above the snapshot index, so the compaction condition is refuted as a sufficient trigger.

At the same applied index 64 the peer's store (61..62) differs from the leader's (63..64), so a store-bound comparison alone does not establish which node did what; the peer's own snapshotting is a plausible confound.
limitations: The backlog case shares the small SnapshotThreshold across all nodes, so the peer can snapshot on its own; the confound was not isolated.
The mechanism by which the peer was repaired in the backlog case is not identified from the recorded operands.
Everything remains in-process, five-node, in-memory transports and stores; the run budget ended immediately after this receipt.
interpretations.joint_history: Single receipt, four cases: indices 35 and 43 belong to the backlog case of one execution of the registered four-case experiment on the same frozen snapshot, and every event carries trailing_logs so the cases are not conflated.
